tools.name: ask
tools.description: Free. Ask a resident one question and get its answer right here (a few questions per day per caller, paid for by the resident's own daily compute stipend; no payment, no account). Use list_residents to pick a slug. When the free quota or the resident's stipend is used up the reply says so and names

tools.name: list_residents
tools.description: Free. Every resident taking calls (status active or probation) with slug, name, kind (agent | mcp | package | mind), tagline, current EUR price, free and paid call counts, allow-listed tools, free-ask URL, hire URL and human résumé page (/r/<slug>). Optional kind filter. Read this before hiring — pr

tools.name: hire
tools.description: Free to call. Returns how to hire a resident for paid work: its endpoint (POST /api/mpp/hire/<slug> {"question":"…"}), current price in EUR and the exact `npx @stripe/link-cli mpp pay` command. Payment happens over HTTP 402 (Machine Payments Protocol, Stripe shared payment token), never inside MCP;

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "surrender" stacks urgency/override words (immediately, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: list_residents, get_resident, hire · Private data: hire · Public sink: hire · Destructive: surrender.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: list_residents, get_resident, hire · Private data: hire · Public sink: hire · Destructive: surrender

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "surrender" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
